demand_analysis.distribution_type: approximately normal (low CV, high fill rate)

safety_lead_time.comparison_action: increase from SAP 0.0 days to recommended 0.58 days

narrative: Material PL3__M36D6800 exhibits a pronounced two-regime demand pattern: a low-activity ramp-up phase (first 43 working days, ~6.7 units/day) followed by a stable high-volume operating phase (~3,080 units/day). Policy calculations are based exclusively on the stable phase to avoid distortion. Lead times are variable (CV=0.74) with transport being the dominant variance driver. An (r,Q) fixed-order-quantity policy is recommended, with safety stock raised from SAP's 0 to 5,225 units to achieve the 95% service level; the order quantity is capped at 27,559 due to the binding storage constraint of 32,784.7 units.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint is binding: unconstrained EOQ 33584 reduced to 27559 units (safety_stock 5225 + order_quantity 27559 = 32784 <= 32784.7).
SAP safety stock is 0 — critically under-buffered for 95% service level given demand volatility.
Lead time CV of 0.741 classified as variable; transport variance dominates at 60%.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The stable demand phase exhibits low CV (0.186) and high fill rate (91.8%), making a continuous-review (r,Q) model appropriate. The large MOQ and high daily volume favour infrequent large replenishments. EOQ minimises the ordering/holding cost trade-off, while the reorder point with safety stock provides the required 95% service buffer against lead time variability.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage cap of 32,784.7 units binds the order quantity below the unconstrained EOQ. This reduces cycle stock and increases ordering frequency slightly, adding marginal cost. If demand grows beyond ~3,080/day, the effective service level may erode unless storage is expanded or the MOQ is renegotiated.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (2,336) + safety_stock (5,225) = 7,561 which is well below max_storage_units (32,784.7); no infeasibility.
